title: In-Memory Computing Architecture for Sparse Neural Networks
problem: Processing sparse neural networks during inference requires significant energy due to data movement overhead between memory and compute units. Current architectures fail to efficiently exploit sparsity patterns in neural networks to reduce power consumption.
motivation: Energy efficiency is critical for deploying neural networks at scale, and sparse networks present a major opportunity to reduce inference power consumption.
method: Instead of moving data back and forth between memory and the processor (which wastes energy), this work places compute units directly in the memory. These units exploit sparsity—the presence of many zeros in the network weights and activations—by skipping operations that involve zeros, since multiplying by zero wastes computation. By computing where the data lives, it eliminates the energy-intensive data transfers that dominate inference with sparse neural networks.
key_novelty: Processing units integrated into memory that skip zero-valued operations in sparse neural networks, reducing the energy-intensive data transfers between memory and processor.
contributions: Memory-compute units optimized for sparse neural network inference
PIM architecture exploiting sparsity to reduce energy consumption
45x energy reduction achieved on sparse inference workloads
limitations: Evaluation scope and comparison baselines not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: sparse neural network acceleration via PIM
